# ADR 048 — Exit purges secrets only on a definitely gone lease — consolidated view

## 0. Decision

On `worktree-exit`, after closing the session's row, the hook asks the
backbone whether the exited worktree's task still holds a live lease — one
`GET /api/v1/tasks/<id>`, bounded by the hook's standard 2-second backbone
budget — and purges the task's materialized secrets only on a **definite
"gone"**: the task exists and carries no lease, or the task no longer exists
(404). Every other outcome — a live lease, a timeout, a transport failure, a
5xx, an auth failure — keeps the secrets, and the hook exits successfully
regardless.

This restores spec 017 §3's "exit" trigger with the meaning it always
intended: *on exit, when the lease is gone* — not on every exit, and never on
a guess.

## 1. The problem

017 §3 promises that stale keystore items "are removed by the next local hook
that notices the lease is gone (resume, exit, or `lode doctor`)", and §4
lists `ExitWorktree` among the purge triggers. The first implementation
(WL-36) wired an **unconditional** purge into the exit hook and then removed
it (`3d83856`): 012 §4 designs `ExitWorktree` for one session working several
tasks in sequence, so at exit the lease is normally still held and the
session can come back — an unconditional purge would cost a fresh consent and
a fresh Touch ID on return, which the non-interactive session that is the
common case cannot give.

Since that revert, exit purges **never**, and the code silently diverges from
an accepted spec section. The gap it leaves is the abandoned worktree: one
that is not removed, not `lode worktree done`, not `lode worktree block` — those paths all
purge — but simply left sitting while its lease expires. The server-side
lease sweeper cannot reach a laptop keystore, so live credentials persist on
the machine indefinitely.

The naive fix and the revert were both right about half the problem: exit
must not purge while the lease is held, and exit is still the natural,
automatic point to notice that it is gone. What was missing is the question
in the middle.

## 2. The exit-time lease check

`handleWorktreeExit`, after its existing duty (closing the session row for
the exited lease), makes one best-effort backbone call for the worktree's
bound task: `GET /api/v1/tasks/<id>`. The answer is three-valued, and only
one value purges:

| Backbone answer | Meaning | Action |
|---|---|---|
| `200`, `lease` absent/null | Task exists, no live lease — expired or released | **Purge** |
| `404` | Task no longer exists (deleted, spec 044) | **Purge** |
| `200`, live lease present | Session can come back; ceremony products still needed | Keep |
| Timeout, connection failure, 5xx | The backbone did not answer the question | Keep, warn |
| `401`/`403`, undecodable body | The *client* is broken, not the lease | Keep, warn |

Three rules carry the design:

- **Uncertainty never purges.** Only the two definite answers in the first
  rows purge. A `401` says the token is wrong, a `5xx` or a timeout says
  nothing at all — none of them says "gone". A secret reaped by mistake costs
  a whole consent ceremony and a Touch ID to restore, which the returning
  non-interactive session cannot give; a secret kept one hook longer costs
  nothing.
- **A live lease keeps, whoever holds it.** No holder comparison: a re-claim
  after expiry binds a fresh worktree (normally on another machine), and
  distinguishing "our lease" from "someone else's" buys nothing worth the
  complexity — the stale items still fall to this worktree's next
  gone-answered exit or to removal.
- **The hook never fails its event.** The check shares the hook package's
  existing 2-second per-call backbone budget (`backboneTimeout`) — exit
  already makes an `EndAgentSession` call under the same bound, so the worst
  case adds one bounded round trip to an event that is already
  network-touching. One attempt, no retry; any failure is a warning on
  stderr and a successful exit.

Ordering: 017's rule that the purge is local-only and "runs before any
backbone call" belongs to the **unconditional** triggers — worktree removal,
`lode worktree done`, `lode worktree block` — where the worktree's life is ending and the purge
must happen regardless of connectivity. On exit the purge is conditional *on*
a backbone answer by design, so it necessarily follows one; a purge skipped
for lack of an answer is deferred to the next trigger, not lost.

## 3. Degradation

The "lease expires, worktree remains" row of 017 §6 becomes: items persist
until the next hook that gets a definite "gone" — in practice the next exit
of that worktree — or until `/lode-resume` re-materializes, or until worktree
removal purges unconditionally. A server unreachable at exit leaves the items
in place with a warning; nothing blocks, nothing prompts.

## 4. Consequences

**Exit gains a bounded backbone dependency.** One extra round trip, capped at
2 seconds, on an event that already talks to the backbone under the same cap.
Accepted deliberately: reaping at the natural trigger, automatically, is
worth a bounded slow-network delay on an interactive worktree switch.

**The purge on exit is best-effort by construction.** A laptop that is
offline every time a worktree is exited never reaps that worktree's items
until removal. That is the intended trade — availability of the hook's own
event always wins.

**A worktree nobody touches again is still not reached.** Exit fires when a
session leaves; a worktree that is abandoned *and never entered or exited
again* fires no hook, so its items persist until removal. This ADR narrows
the abandoned-worktree window to "until the next visit"; it cannot close a
window no hook can see.

**The residual is closed by a sweep, decided in WL-257.** `lode doctor` walks
the machine's local manifests, asks the backbone about each task's lease, and
purges on the same definite answers §2 defines, with the same rule that
uncertainty never purges. It needs no hook to fire, which is what makes it
reach a worktree nobody enters, exits, or removes. 017 §4 states it; this ADR
keeps the exit-time half, which reaps at the natural trigger without waiting
for a human to run a diagnostic.

## 5. Rejected alternatives

- **Give the sweep to `lode doctor` instead.** A manual diagnostic reaps only
  when a human remembers to run it; the common case would keep credentials
  for days. Rejected as the closer for this gap — exit is automatic and
  already fires at the right moment. (A doctor sweep may still be worth
  having for the never-visited residual above; that is a separate, open
  decision.)
- **Amend 017 §4 to drop exit from the trigger list.** Ratifies the
  divergence instead of closing it, and leaves the abandoned-worktree gap
  standing with removal as the only reaper. Rejected.
- **Purge unconditionally on exit.** Tried by WL-36 and reverted; breaks the
  012 §4 multi-task session. Not reconsidered.
